scope: Source-only frozen review. No source, state, lease, environment, MPS, checkpoint loading, training, probe, or pyc writes.

advisories.summary: retained_failed_attempts resolution labels do not match the logs they cite.
advisories.detail: preflight-attempt-01.log ends with 'ValueError: Full audit candidate set differs', but the receipt labels it an inherited runtime-continuity pin defect. preflight-attempt-02.log shows 'registration valid; pins=13786', i.e. it passed, but the receipt labels it a full-audit label mismatch. The runtime-continuity traceback actually lives in top-level preflight.log (mtime 22:38), which the receipt does not list. cpu-restore-attempt-02 and -03 labels also differ from their logs (SyntaxError and 'Saved endpoint metadata and receipt wall fields differ'). The receipt cites 5 failures while attempts/ holds 18 logs, of which 13 are unlisted (passing or later runs).
advisories.failure_scenario: A later auditor reads the receipt, maps preflight-attempt-02 to a fixed defect, and cannot reproduce that fix from the cited log. No runtime effect.
advisories.recommended_action: Write a new accounting note (do not edit the receipt) mapping each attempts/*.log to its real outcome and noting that top-level preflight.log is superseded.

advisories.summary: validate_runtime_continuity compares a tree with itself, so its byte-by-byte member check is vacuous.
advisories.detail: registration.json runtime_continuity.source_runtime_root and runtime_root both resolve to .../D2-gradient-capsule-parent-freeze-20261025-r5/own/runtime. old_files and new_files are therefore the same files, and the per-member equality check cannot fail on tampering. The fail-closed binding still holds through verify_pins (current bytes == pins), the pinned-member digest == runtime_sha256 == PARENT_RUNTIME_SHA (2cf10e9f...), and the 13786-pin registration. Tamper-detection therefore rests on pins plus the runtime digest, not on the continuity comparison as written.
advisories.failure_scenario: Runtime member bytes change and the pins are regenerated together. The continuity check still passes, and only the runtime_sha256 digest (which would then change) catches it. Shown only by reading code, not by running it.
advisories.recommended_action: Optional: point the continuity check at the archival source root, or drop the byte comparison and keep the explicit runtime digest check. Not required for this launch.
